messages:
Chris Nguyen: Quick follow-up from today’s infra segment — dropping a short thread to capture APAC timing, routing fallbacks, and autoscaler questions.
Olivia Park: APAC question: if compute arrives in late Q3 but interconnects lag, can we accept compute-only and enable limited service?
Chris Nguyen: Yes, we can stage compute-only zones. Networking features (private interconnects) would come later; we’d mark those zones as limited and only route non-sensitive traffic.
Leo Zhang: Autoscaler: will the canary let us test region-scoped policies? I want to ensure changes don't flip globally.
Chris Nguyen: Canary is region-scoped. We will flip flags per-region and have automatic rollback on key regressions.
Anika Bose: If GPU supply tight, what9s our prioritized routing sequence for Hosted customers?
Chris Nguyen: Priority sequence: 1) model-variant fallback (smaller/quantized), 2) intra-region queueing with degraded context, 3) cross-region routing for opt-in customers.
Infra Bot: deploy-bot: canary-autoscaler rollout started 2026-08-11T15:02Z for 3 clusters in us-east-1.
Maya Lopez: Request: Product needs a one-paragraph customer note describing cross-region fallback latency expectations. Who owns?
David Romero: Legal/Customer Success should review; David will sync with Maya for wording and contract implications.
Chris Nguyen: Action items: I’ll post a short owner matrix by EOD Thursday. Leo will own SLO dashboard work. David + Maya to draft customer messaging. Closing thread when the doc is live.
